So the losses are not unexpected. Yet Trump’s midterm losses may rival the cataclysmic losses of Clinton in 1994 and Obama in 2010 (both of whom ironically left office with the highest ratings of their presidencies). Saving midterm congressional seats is always hard for an incumbent president. 2) Trump’s last two years : The blue wave will give the extremist left enormous momentum. But if the last two years of the Clinton and Obama administrations (both of which had earlier lost their initial House and Senate majorities) are any guide, it won’t radically derail Trump’s last two-year initiatives—since it is still unlikely Democrats will gain a veto-proof Senate. Except for judicial and cabinet nominations, which will all be blocked, Trump will continue Obama-like, pen and phone, executive-order domestic policies. Senate races in North Carolina and Ohio were high-profile contests, but each amounted to a competition over purple territory. Georgia, which Trump won in 2024, gave Democratic senator Jon Ossoff an easy reelection victory and elected the first black governor in its history, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms.
